ai.title: Add carve-based eval pipeline to evalbuff
ai.summary: evalbuff now supports carve-based evaluation via `carve-features.ts` and `run-carve-eval.ts`, which analyze a codebase to identify features, generate diffs that delete them, and run agents to rebuild them against ground truth. This replaces the previous git-commit-based eval approach. The `ClaudeRunner` now accepts a configurable `model` argument (defaulting to `claude-opus-4-5-20251101`), and `openai` v6.33.0 is added to `evalbuff`'s dependencies.

eli5.text: evalbuff can now test an AI coding assistant in a new way: instead of comparing whole code snapshots, it picks a specific feature, deletes just that feature, and asks an AI to rebuild it from a plain-language description, then judges the result against the original. This affects anyone running or improving evalbuff's evaluation harness, who will see carve-based eval tasks and a configurable assistant model option. The feature-level delete-and-rebuild loop and model selection are live today, backed by two new scripts and one adjusted runner.

ai.title: CLI terminal reset and error propagation fixes
ai.summary: CLI wrapper and renderer now enforce terminal state reset (alternate screen, mouse, cursor) on SIGKILL or fatal errors. `renderer-cleanup.ts` exports `TERMINAL_RESET_SEQUENCES` for reuse in `cli/release/index.js` and `freebuff/cli/release/index.js`. Early `uncaughtException` handlers in `cli/src/index.tsx` ensure errors print to the main screen before renderer init. Wrapper update logic uses `once('exit')` and explicit `resetTerminal()` calls to prevent state leakage.

eli5.text: If the assistant app gets forcefully killed while running in your terminal, the terminal can get stuck in a weird state where things like your cursor disappear or keyboard shortcuts stop working normally. Now, a background monitoring process that stays running will automatically reset your terminal to normal whenever this happens, even if the main app can't clean up after itself. You would notice this as your terminal returning to normal behavior immediately after a crash, instead of staying visually broken until you manually reset it.

The FAQ and philosophy sections now list 9 specialized helpers that the assistant can use, including a new one called thinker-gpt that connects to your ChatGPT account for deeper reasoning. The way to do big tasks from start to finish is also spelled out more clearly with the /interview → /plan → (implement) → /review commands, and some of the text on the page uses a slightly lighter color. If you look at the homepage now, you'll see the updated descriptions with clearer bullet points and slightly brighter text.

Previously, the unhovered label appeared dimmed or faded; now it displays at normal brightness. This only affects how the stop button looks in the command-line interface, and you can see the difference right away the next time you use it.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.637 release bundles evals, terminal cleanup, UI copy
ai.summary: Version 1.0.637 rolls up the same-day changes: the carve-based eval pipeline in `evalbuff` (carve-features.ts, run-carve-eval.ts, configurable ClaudeRunner model defaulting to claude-opus-4-5-20251101, openai v6.33.0); CLI terminal reset and error propagation fixes (renderer-cleanup.ts exports TERMINAL_RESET_SEQUENCES, early uncaughtException handlers in cli/src/index.tsx, once('exit')/resetTerminal() in the wrapper); Home page FAQ/philosophy copy updates in home-client.tsx; and the StopButton idle contrast change in cli/src/components/stop-button.tsx. Tool executor error messages now append the original tool call input (truncated at 500 chars) via packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts, and the AgentChildrenGrid useMemo hook moved above early returns to satisfy Rules of Hooks.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json: version field changed from 1.0.636 to 1.0.637 in a single-line diff. Release instructions indicate this row is a version bump summarizing user-visible features, model changes, and CLI improvements shipped since 1.0.636.

eli5.text: This release makes your AI coding assistant smarter at checking its own work, more reliable when things go wrong, and easier to read in the terminal. The big addition is a new built-in evaluation system that automatically tests how well the assistant rebuilds features after they are deleted, using the latest Claude model by default, so the tool constantly gets better at recovering from mistakes. Error messages now include the actual command that failed, truncated to keep things readable, which makes debugging much faster when a tool call breaks. The terminal interface now cleanly resets its display mode when you quit or when it crashes, preventing a garbled screen, and the stop button is easier to see when it is just sitting there waiting. On the home screen and FAQ, the copy now highlights the 9 specialized subagents and explains the slash commands more clearly. Upgrading gives you a more self-improving assistant, cleaner error handling, a polished terminal experience, and a friendlier home screen that tells you what the tool can actually do.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.27 ships carve-based eval, terminal reset fixes, tool
ai.summary: Version 0.0.27 bundles the carve-based eval pipeline added to evalbuff, the earlier CLI terminal reset and error propagation fixes, and the stop button contrast raise. The tool executor now appends truncated (JSON-stringified, 500-char capped) input to error messages from packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts, and message-with-agents.tsx fixed a React hook order violation in AgentChildrenGrid. These changes ship across Web, CLI, and Desktop in this packaging commit.
ai.evidence: freebuff/cli/release/package.json line 3: version changed from "0.0.26" to "0.0.27".

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.27 upgrades how AI coding agents are tested against real codebases and makes the terminal experience more reliable when things go wrong. The headline addition is a new evaluation pipeline that analyzes a project, removes a feature it finds, and checks whether an AI agent can rebuild that feature correctly. Tool errors now include a readable snippet of what the AI tried to do, so it's easier to understand why something failed. The terminal now properly resets when the program crashes or is killed, preventing garbled screens and stray cursors. The on-screen stop button is more visible when idle, and the web homepage now highlights 9 specialized subagents plus updated FAQ text. Upgrading gives you clearer error messages when AI tools fail, cleaner terminal behavior during crashes, and a more robust system for testing agent accuracy against real coding tasks.

ai.title: Add retrieval-led reasoning note to AGENTS.md
ai.summary: AGENTS.md now prioritizes retrieval-led reasoning over pre-training-led reasoning, instructing agents to read relevant docs before implementation. Doc links in the file were simplified from markdown links to plain text paths. evalbuff/src/run-carve-eval.ts added helpers to track and merge doc file reads from agent traces, exposing `docsRead` in `CarveEvalResult`.

eli5.text: The internal instructions that guide the coding assistant were updated so it now tells the assistant to look at relevant reference materials first before trying to write new code, rather than relying on what it already knows. The list of reference materials was also reformatted from clickable links to plain text file paths. At the same time, a behind-the-scenes measurement tool was extended so it can count how often the assistant opened those reference documents during a task and add up the totals across multiple attempts. The measurement change is in place today and nothing depends on it yet, so no results are visible from it right now, but the new instruction for the assistant is live and applies to anyone the assistant is helping.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs its automated test comparisons inside a project, it now makes a shortcut so it can instantly read the shared instructions file without any setup. The assistant also keeps a running tally of which instruction files it has looked at during each test pass, printing that tally at the end, making it easier to confirm it actually reviewed the right guidance while the tests run.
